assign.title: The popup's real cause, found and fixed — plus a repo-wide guard
assign.outcome:
**What landed** — the popup wasn't a Node `spawn()` bug (every `detached:true, windowsHide:true` spawn tested, even from a genuinely console-less parent, showed 0 visible windows in repeated `EnumWindows` probes). The real cause: the Windows logon task that boots Servex runs `powershell.exe -WindowStyle Hidden` — and PowerShell hides its own window a moment *after* Windows already shows it, a proven flash (reproduced by triggering the real task and watching a real `powershell.exe` window appear). The fix — `Servex/hidden-launch.vbs`, run through `wscript.exe`, which never has a console at all — is proven with the same probe: 0 visible windows.

- [x] why we still get these terminal popups: root-caused and reproduced on demand — see the `decision` line in this task's log
- [x] make them hidden please: `Servex/hidden-launch.vbs` proven at 0 visible windows; `Servex/readme.md`'s scheduled-task instructions now use it
- [x] fix every launcher found: swept 17 files ([`Server/window-lint.mjs`](/framework/ai2/2026-09-28/hidden-windows/)'s repo-wide scan found 34 real gaps; 8 remain, all confirmed false positives — a same-named method definition, or the words "Start-Process"/"fork" in prose — logged one by one in this task's log)
- [x] enforce it: `.claude/hooks/syntax-guard.mjs`'s `hidden_guard` is now a per-CALL check (was a rough file-wide count) and names the `detached:true`-with-no-`windowsHide` shape specifically; hand-tested live (a bad scratch call blocked the write, the fixed version did not) — plus the standing `Server/window-lint.mjs` sweep tool for a repo-wide check anytime

**One thing only the owner can finish** — re-pointing the LIVE scheduled task at the new wrapper needs the login password (`schtasks`/`Register-ScheduledTask` asked for it; backed off rather than guess at it). The exact one-paste PowerShell command is now in [`Servex/readme.md`](/framework/servex/), "Surviving a reboot" section — run it once, no code change needed.

**Left as-is, on purpose:** `Servex/Process.js` and `Servex/sustain.mjs`'s own internal spawns still carry their original "inherits the parent's hidden console" reasoning (now with `windowsHide: true` added too, belt-and-braces) — that design is sound once the boot chain above is fixed, and didn't need re-architecting.

built Server/window-watch.mjs (modeled on Servex/Monitor.js's proven one-hidden-PowerShell-loop pattern, never a new PowerShell per sample): one long-lived hidden PS child does EnumWindows+IsWindowVisible every 1s, seeds a baseline of every window already open at start so nothing pre-existing counts as new, then on a genuinely new visible window whose owning process image is conhost/cmd/powershell/node/bash/claude, walks the parent chain up to 6 hops via Win32_Process and prints one JSON line; Node timestamps it (append.mjs's own local-offset ISO shape) and appends to C:/Users/mike/AppData/Local/lew42/servex/logs/windows.jsonl, creating the dir if missing. Never crashes: PS child restart-on-exit with backoff, Node's own append wrapped in try/catch.

boot-tested it in the foreground first (node Server/window-watch.mjs, ~24s): started cleanly, exactly one PowerShell child, zero false-positive hits from the baseline pass, no crash/restart line; killed that test instance before the real launch.

started the real instance HIDDEN via Servex/orphan.mjs (the exact pattern Servex uses for the gate and every dev server: a short-lived PowerShell's Start-Process -WindowStyle Hidden launches cmd.exe /d /s /c "node Server/window-watch.mjs >> out 2>> err", so it outlives whoever started it and is out of reach of a tree-kill) — orphan pid 23620 (cmd.exe) -> node.exe pid 46396 -> its own hidden powershell.exe probe pid 43868.

PROOF it's hidden: a fresh EnumWindows/IsWindowVisible PowerShell probe took a snapshot of all visible top-level windows (9), ran the hidden launch above, then sampled every 250ms for 10s unioning any handle seen visible that wasn't in the before-set (catches a flash even between two samples, not just a start/end diff). Result: 0 new visible windows. Left running on purpose — that's the whole point, it needs to be watching when the next real popup happens. pid 46396 (node.exe) is the one to find it again; its cmd.exe parent is pid 23620.
